title: Deleting ~/.cache breaks all future backups with no apparant fix
body:
Some time ago I deleted my ~/.cache directory since my drive was full and a cache, by definition, should just slow things down if it's gone as it's regenerated. If it is the only place that some vital data is stored or this is otherwise not the case, then it isn't a cache and thus does not belong in ~/.cache. Despite this, after deleting it, borg won't backup anymore. Instead it says the following. I tried mkdir -p ~/.cache/borg, which had no effect. Instead, Borg should notice that the cache has been cleared and regenerate whatever it needs. 


comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Before we start debugging a potentially long-fixed bug, you could first try to reproduce this issue with something more recent (like 1.4.x or 1.2.x) from one of these sources:

- https://launchpad.net/~costamagnagianfranco/+archive/ubuntu/borgbackup (from borg ubuntu/debian maintainer)
- https://github.com/borgbackup/borg/releases (fat binaries from here, you could start with 1.2.4 from here)

Please note that when crossing the 1.2.4 / 1.2.5 version boundary, you MUST read and follow the CVE-related instructions at top of the changelog.

When you upgrade to Ubuntu 24.04 at some time, you would also get a more recent borg version (1.2.8).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
How risky is the CVE update procedure when my current borg instance is broken like this? 

Also, does it store any data outside of the archive and the ~/.cache directory? If so, deleting that may make sense. It would seem to think that the ~/.cache directory exists, so there should be some easy way to convince it otherwise (like if I was backing up after reinstalling my OS).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
At first, you would just use the more recent release to reproduce the bug (or see that it is fixed).

If it is not fixed, you could just delete the cache: `borg delete --cache-only REPO`

The cache can be rebuilt, it just will need some time.

You can do some harmless operations like `borg list` or so, but do **NOT** run `borg check --repair` with a 1.2.5+ release before doing the upgrade steps from the changelog.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
OK, so break-lock worked, but didn't change your issue.

borg needs the chunks cache (chunks index), it can't work without it.

And usually it creates the directories fine (and rebuilds the caches from the repo) when the cache is missing, so I suggest you do:
```
rm -rf /home/<censored>/.cache/borg/422b7ed27b0022a878085cea02af612dff14f0d9ba0bbe4f5edc78af342dcc10
```

And then run `borg create` exactly as you normally do when running your backups. Don't mix up users/permissions.

comments.author: reporter

I bought my off-site server back home so I can just delete the old archives and make a new one. I thought that this would solve the issue, but it did not. Even with a completely new repository made by `borg init` and cleared ~/.cache on both the server and client, I still get the same sort of errors.

Where else does borg store state? I want to completely nuke the state that borg stores so it just starts fresh. I do not have any more patience for further debugging of this issue. I need my backups to work again with minimal fuss.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
borg separates caches/configs for different repos by putting the repo id into the cache/config file path. thus, if you create and use a new repo, that is a fresh start (as far as borg state is concerned).

did you try a recent borg version meanwhile? just so that we don't hunt bugs that are long fixed already.

i would need more information to reproduce / debug this issue.

or alternatively, access to the misbehaving installation (e.g. via ssh) to reproduce/debug it there.

comments.author: participant2

Some ideas for next test (after fsck):
- no sudo user switching, either use a local root or normal user shell
- no BORG_* env vars set (except BORG_REPO and BORG_PASSPHRASE if you need those)
- no borg wrappers or scripts, just invoke borg directly from a shell
- `id` invocation and output
- `borg -V` invocation and output
- `borg create ...` invocation and output (including traceback)
- if you get "no such file" again: `ls -ld DIR` for each parent dir of the path it complains about, starting from /
